options.plan: Upstream release 26.8.0; commercial support not assessed
options.region: Operator-selected hosting; storage destinations not verified
options.configuration: Confidential service account; client_credentials; client_secret_basic only; scoped roles/audience; default no refresh

conditions: Limit this proposal to bearer access tokens obtained by a confidential machine client for a separately identified resource API. OAuth client_credentials acts for the client itself, not an end user; it is not OIDC login, an ID Token or delegated user access.

Configure a narrowly scoped API audience through reviewed client-role Audience Resolve or an explicit Audience mapper. The requesting client ID is not automatically the API audience; a realm role alone does not establish a target service, and a scope string alone does not grant a role.

The resource API must validate the selected realm issuer, trusted signature/key and algorithm, expiry, intended audience and its required permissions, then bind the service principal to authorized resources. Reject a missing or foreign audience, missing role or unknown resource context; issuance alone is not authorization.

Review disabled-client behavior and already issued tokens separately: new role/audience mappings change future tokens, but an existing access token can remain valid until expiry. No live token issuance, API validation, immediate revocation or deployed enforcement was tested.

This release-pinned scope does not inherit browser/native clients, organization memberships, enterprise brokers, SCIM, residency or human authentication controls. Hosting, operations and cost remain unverified.

evidence.summary: The pinned audience guide describes bearer tokens for resource services, role-based or explicit audience mapping, service-side audience checks and already-issued-token caveats. Proposed OPTIONAL is restricted API-token context, not verified runtime authorization or revocation.

conditions: Use a separate confidential OIDC client registration with Client authentication On and Service account roles enabled. POST grant_type=client_credentials to the selected realm token endpoint; no browser redirect, user password, user consent or user-delegation flow is selected.

Select Client ID and Secret and restrict Allowed authentication method to Authorization: Basic as documented at https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/4246609cf2024c85016d3fb1254c3d2533367c31/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/clients/oidc/con-confidential-client-credentials.adoc. Basic encoding is not encryption: protect transport with TLS and keep the secret server-side, outside browser bundles, URLs and logs.

Token roles are the intersection of assigned service-account roles and explicit role scope mappings, including linked client scopes. Do not enable deprecated Full Scope Allowed or grant realm-management roles as a shortcut; exact least-privilege roles and resource authorization need independent review.

Retain the documented default without a refresh token or Keycloak user session: obtain a new access token after expiry, and do not imply browser logout or user offboarding semantics. The example's lifetime is not a guaranteed deployment setting; inspect the configured token lifespan and any changed refresh/session behavior.

Signed JWT, federated client assertions, mTLS and sender-constrained tokens are separate configurations, not implied by this shared-secret scope. No client, credentials, role assignments, secret rotation, provider deployment or live machine request was created or tested.

evidence.summary: The pinned service-account guide documents confidential client prerequisites, client_credentials, default Basic client authentication, role-scope intersection and default access-token-only behavior. Proposed SUPPORTED remains conditional and unreviewed, not a verified machine integration.
